turns.assessment: The event is a hard bidirectional optical loss on the S14–S04 cable segment: OSC is lost on the first outbound span (O126) and reciprocal last inbound span (O125), while the downstream inline amplifier and inbound preamp report loss. Stable pump currents and unchanged upstream amplifier telemetry argue against amplifier failure. The simultaneous analogous losses toward S20 suggest excavation or duct damage near S14 affecting multiple cables, strongly favoring a fibre cut.

proposals.rationale: E23 is the S14-end span of the S14→S04 fibre pair. Its OSC loss, the downstream AMP_INPUT_LOS, and reciprocal-direction OSC/OMS loss precisely localize a bidirectional cable break. A cut also explains complete all-channel loss and the simultaneous impact on every affected service.
A sufficiently severe bend, crushed cable, or splice damage could lose both traffic and OSC, but the abrupt complete bidirectional loss and concurrent failure of another S14 cable favor a cut.
A pulled S14 OMS input patch could remove outbound channels, but it does not adequately explain reciprocal OSC loss on the line span and the matching S14–S20 failures.
